gaps.sentence: The new manager wants to back ___ the sales team's proposal.
gaps.explanation: back up = support (a person, plan); also make a copy of data.

gaps.sentence: The car ___ down on the motorway and had to be towed.
She ___ down an offer from a rival university.
They've just moved ___ to their new flat.
gaps.explanation: move in = start living in a new home.

gaps.sentence: We had to call ___ the order because the kitchen had closed.
Don't ___ up all the milk — we need some for breakfast.
gaps.explanation: use up = finish the whole supply of something.

gaps.sentence: After twenty years of smoking, he finally managed to give it ___.
gaps.explanation: give up = stop/quit (a habit or attempt).

gaps.sentence: Wake ___ — you'll be late for school!
